Thanks again for the demo last week — Octavia is excited to move forward with a Dedicated GPU pool for our inference workloads. Before the SOW signature we want to align on regional capacity priorities and bursting constraints so we can finalize operational runbooks. High level:

- Initial regions: us-west-2 primary, eu-west-1 secondary (we may expand APAC Q4).
- Target baseline throughput: ~450 QPS for short text generation (p95 token latency target ~120ms).
- Expected spiky bursts (product launches): short spikes up to 2.5x baseline for ~45-90 minutes, ~4–6 times per month.

Questions for your team:
1) Can you confirm recommended GPU types for the baseline vs burst headroom?
2) How do autoscale policies handle rapid bursts vs gradual growth — any cool-downs we should tune?
3) Are there hard limits on regional burst capacity or cross-region fallback we should plan for?

I've attached our initial capacity estimates and the draft SOW (v2). Can we schedule a 30–45m ops handshake this week to lock the playbook and launch window? Rajiv (ops) and I are available Thu/Fri afternoon PST.

Best,
Lisa Park

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. This thread is now the working ops handshake for Octavia's Dedicated launch.

Quick answers up front, and then I'll propose an agenda and owners for the call:

- GPU recommendation: for your baseline profile (steady 450 QPS, 120ms p95) we recommend an M60-ish class for cost-efficiency (quantized FP16 workflows). For burst headroom we suggest reserving a pool of A10/A100-similar instances you can spill into — we'll call this the "burst tranche." We'll include explicit fallback pairs (e.g., us-west-2: A10 primary, fallback to us-west-1/AZ crossover).
- Autoscale behavior: Redwood's autoscaler supports aggressive scale-up (<90s) with a conservative cool-down (5–15m) on scale-down to avoid oscillation during repeated microbursts. For your pattern (45–90m bursts) we'd set a short scale-up window plus a 10m scale-down to maintain headroom during rolling traffic.
- Hard limits / cross-region fallback: there are no hard-account limits, but burst capacity depends on regional inventory. We'll surface a regional capacity SLA in the playbook and configure automatic cross-region fallback when local headroom is <30% for 5 consecutive minutes.

Proposed ops handshake (30m):
1) Confirm GPU SKU mapping + quantization profile (Ben)
2) Autoscale cadence and cool-downs (Marcus)
3) Regional priority & fallback rules + runbook triggers (Grace)
4) SOW next steps + DocuSign timeline (Naomi)

Available windows (Thu/Fri PST): Thu 1:00–3:30pm, Fri 2:00–4:30pm. Which works?

Thanks — I'll pull together a short slide with proposed numeric thresholds and a draft runbook.

—Naomi Feldman

Hi all — jumping in on GPU sizing and performance assumptions.

Notes from bench runs with models similar to Octavia's:
- M60-class (32GB quantized) handles ~80–110 concurrent short-gen sessions per card at your latency target when KV cache hit-rate is >85%. Good for steady baseline.
- A10 (or analogous) provides ~2.5–3x throughput per card for short sequences; excellent for burst tranche.

Operational recommendations:
- Start with baseline pool sized for ~1.2x your target (i.e., capacity for 540 QPS) to avoid constant autoscale churn.
- Pre-warm burst tranche to a small standby level (10–15% of expected burst headroom) during known launch windows (we can automate via scheduled scale policies).
- Implement prefix/KV caching on the Redwood side for common prompts to reduce token costs and raise effective throughput.

I've uploaded a small regional-capacity-matrix CSV (attached) with candidate SKU mixes per region and cost delta estimates.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: regional-capacity-matrix.csv

Lisa / team — a couple of operational constraints to call out so expectations are aligned:

1) Regional inventory windows: EU capacity is slightly constrained in the first two weeks of July due to provider maintenance windows. If Octavia needs firm fallbacks into eu-west-1 during July launches we should either pre-book burst capacity (reserve) or plan a controlled cross-region failover to us-west-2.
2) Network egress: cross-region fallback will add ~30–80ms overhead to token round-trips depending on path — include that in SLA conversations if p95 must hold for all requests.
3) Autoscale policy specifics: we'll create two policies — "scheduled pre-warm" (time-based, for launch events) and "reactive burst" (signal-based, rapid scale-up). Reactive policy will be aggressive on scale-up but capped at a configurable % of total pre-booked burst capacity to avoid accidental exhaustion.

Action items I can own before the call:
- Draft the fallback runbook (failover triggers, rollback criteria, comms playbook).
- Produce a small inventory risk note for EU for your legal and procurement teams.

I'll attach the draft fallback runbook as a short MD in the shared drive after this thread.

—Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Ops, Redwood Inference
